question: Can a complete G0-G4 incumbent, built before PrefixGraph, safely terminate provably non-publishable PrefixGraph anchors early enough to reduce complete canonical create cost without changing bytes, tie law, locality, or memory ownership?
baseline: Canonical promoted r25 uses prefixgraph_process_isolation=True in the rebound release-candidate path; PrefixGraph child completes/exits before G0-G4. PrefixGraph only publishes when pg_bytes < g04_bytes; equal bytes retain G0-G4.
mechanism: Reverse only the inner construction order for the experiment: build unchanged complete G0-G4 first, then run PrefixGraph with the existing exact lower-bound probe using complete g04_bytes as an external incumbent. Terminate an anchor when immutable framing plus already-forced exact payload bytes >= g04_bytes, because equality cannot publish PrefixGraph under current cross-representation tie law.
